text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bunds, futures sink to new session lows in late trade on weaker U.S. debt prices and profit-taking after Friday's gains. Dec Bund support at 99.10, resistance 99.73. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.26, down 0.44 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts trapped in consolidation phase on Monday with weaker-than-expected UK industrial production data giving just a fleeting boost to a market plagued by uncertainty ahead of Conservative Party Conference which kicks off tomorrow. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-18/32, down 08/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - December bond future ends steady, outperforms Bunds. Cash spds narrow along curve, ongoing domestic demand helps. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 125.84 down 0.04 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended firmer but were off session highs in a market lacking concrete direction following last week's meteoric gains on euphoria about Italy's 1997 budget for Europe. Market rebounded at open after late Friday bout of profit-taking, but sentiment somewhat depressed by lower T-bonds and bunds and gains were pared throughout session. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.29 up 0.19 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries linger in slightly negative territory in extremely thin mid-morning trade after overseas profits taken. Consumer credit at 1500 EDT only Monday data on calendar. Market preparing for Tuesday's 10-yr note sale. When-issued 10-yr note yielding 6.4875 pct.The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-10/32, down 12/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.77 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended up on Monday, but came off the day's highs on a U.S. news agency report quoting a senior LDP official as saying a rise in the official discount rate will probably be considered after general elections. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.90, down 0.50 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - New issue activity was wide-ranging on Monday as the Eurobond market quickly got back into its stride after the U.S. jobs-induced hiatus of late last week. Wachovia Bank of North Carolina emerged with a $250 million 12-year deal at a 43 basis points spread over U.S. Treasuries. The borrower launched a $500 million five-year FRN in May to general acclaim. But a two-year $100 million fixed-rate deal in July was a slower-moving transaction. Dealers said the target audience for the short-dated deal was unfamiliar with the name.
